cards.text: Jesus is in Jerusalem now, and He walks into the temple courts. There are people in there selling. In the TEMPLE, friend.

cards.question: Jesus walks into the temple courts and finds people selling there. What does He do?

answers.text: He begins to drive them out
He asks the priests about it

cards.text: And Jesus doesn't just drive them out. He tells them what's written in Scripture about God's house.

cards.question: Jesus quotes Scripture to the sellers: God's house will be a house of ___.
God's house is meant to be a house of prayer. What does Jesus tell the sellers they've made it?

cards.text: After that, Jesus is teaching at the temple EVERY day. But the chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people are intent on killing Him.

cards.question: The chief priests, scribes and leaders of the people want to kill Jesus. Why can't they find a way to do it?

answers.text: All the people hang on His words
His disciples stand guard around Him

cards.text: One day Jesus is teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, when up walk the chief priests, the scribes AND the elders. That's not a visit, friend. That's the whole group chat showing up in person.

cards.question: The chief priests, scribes and elders walk up to Jesus in the temple courts. What do they demand to know?

answers.text: By what authority He does these things
Which teacher trained Him in the law
How long He plans to stay in the city

cards.text: They came to put Jesus on the spot. He doesn't hand them an answer. He tells them He's got a question for them too.

cards.question: Jesus has a question of His own for the chief priests, scribes and elders. What's it about?

cards.text: That's John the Baptist, who went all around the Jordan preaching a baptism of repentance (Luke 3:3). Jesus asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men.
The leaders huddle up and talk it over among themselves. Like coworkers trying to word a reply to the boss so it doesn't come back on them.

cards.question: The leaders figure that if they say John's baptism was from heaven, Jesus will ask why they didn't believe John.
If the leaders say John's baptism was from men, they'll have trouble with the crowd, because the people are convinced John was a ___.
If the leaders say John's baptism was from men, what do they think the people will do to them?

cards.text: From heaven gets them in trouble with Jesus. From men gets them in trouble with the crowd. So they go looking for a way out.

cards.question: Stuck between two answers they don't like, what do the leaders finally tell Jesus about John's baptism?
Since the leaders won't say where John's baptism came from, Jesus goes ahead and tells them where His own authority comes from.

cards.text: Jesus replies, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things." They walked up to put Him on the spot, and somehow THEY'RE the ones standing on it.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of the Scripture Jesus quotes ('My house will be a house of ___'). That tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. Card 3 gives no context that points to 'prayer' over 'learning' or 'music'.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'One day Jesus is teaching…', 'That's not a visit, friend.' and 'That's the whole group chat showing up in person.' Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'They came to put Jesus on the spot' adds a motive for the leaders' approach. Luke 20:1-2 says they came up and asked about His authority. The text never says why they came.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This card retells Luke 20:5-6, which cards 14 to 16 have already covered. It does not move the passage forward.
This story card is three sentences: 'From heaven gets them in trouble with Jesus.', 'From men gets them in trouble with the crowd.' and 'So they go looking for a way out.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 17 says both answers get the leaders in trouble and that they look for a way out. The question itself then says 'Stuck between two answers they don't like'. Together these rule out both wrong answers, 'That it was from heaven' and 'That it was from men', and leave only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'They walked up to put Him on the spot' adds a motive for the leaders' approach. The text never states one.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
